hypothesis: If paired bovid horns are conjugate mirror-image spirals, then after reflecting one horn across the skull's midsagittal plane, its fitted spiral parameters (pitch, radius, and handedness) match the other horn's within measurement and fluctuating-asymmetry error.
pass_criterion: In at least 90% of adult individuals of spiral-horned bovid species, the mirror-reflected left-horn centreline, fitted by a helico-spiral or logarithmic spiral, matches the right-horn centreline. The match requires opposite handedness, a left/right difference in fitted growth rate or pitch below 10%, and a mean residual distance between the reflected and actual horn centrelines below 5% of horn length.
fail_criterion: The claim fails if opposite handedness is absent in more than 10% of individuals. It also fails if the median left/right difference in fitted spiral parameters exceeds 15%, or if the mean reflected-centreline residual exceeds 10% of horn length, in a majority of species tested.
interpretation: "Conjugate spirals" and "mirror-image" are taken to mean that the left and right horn centrelines, fitted as 3D logarithmic or helico-spirals, are related by reflection across the midsagittal plane. "Hollow-horned ruminants" means Bovidae. Thompson's "symmetry" is read as a statistical match within fluctuating asymmetry, not exact identity. A test needs 3D landmark, semilandmark or mesh data for both horns of the same individual. Linear measurements alone cannot test spiral handedness or curvature.
no_dataset_reason: Three searches found no public dataset I could open and verify that holds 3D geometry for both horns of the same bovid individual. The searches turned up a bighorn sheep horn-length dataset on Dryad that lacks left/right and curvature fields, an Imperial dissertation on bovid horn 3D morphology with restricted access, and papers on cattle skull and goat horn asymmetry that I did not trace to deposited data. I did not fetch any dataset landing page, and naming one unfetched would break the fetch-before-name rule. MorphoSource may hold relevant bovid skull scans, but I could not confirm a specific project or record, so I left the dataset null.
